userStories.title: Expose ticket-title search on the ticket list API
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the optional ticket-list search query and regenerate its OpenAPI/CLI contract.

**Motivation** — Only the agent tool can pass `titleContains`, which the repository already implements as a case-insensitive `contains`.

**Approach** — Apply these Design requirements verbatim:
- `ListTicketsQuery` in `apps/api/src/tickets/dto/list-tickets.query.ts`.
  - Baseline: `status`, `type`, `priority`, `assignedTo`, `unassigned`.
  - Target: it also has `search?: string`, declared with `@ApiPropertyOptional({ maxLength: 100, description: 'Case-insensitive substring of the ticket title' })`, `@IsOptional()`, `@IsString()` and `@MaxLength(100)`.
- `TicketsController.findAll` in `apps/api/src/tickets/tickets.controller.ts`.
  - Baseline: `const { current, size, ...filters } = parseQuery(...)`.
  - Target: `const { current, size, search, ...filters } = parseQuery(...)`. The trimmed `search` is passed as `titleContains` when it is non-empty. A blank or absent `search` passes no `titleContains` key.
  - The route's `@ApiResponse` 400 description becomes 'Invalid filter, search or paging parameter'.
- `TicketListFilterInput` in `apps/api/src/tickets/tickets.service.ts` becomes `Omit<ListTicketsQuery, 'current' | 'size' | 'search'> & { assignedToAgentId?: string; titleContains?: string }`. Three comments change from "only the koda tool search" to "the koda tool search and the REST `search` query": the `TicketListFilterInput` doc comment in `tickets.service.ts`, the `titleContains` field comment in `apps/api/src/tickets/domain/ticket.domain.ts`, and the S5b comment above the `titleContains` line in `findTicketPage` (`prisma-tickets.repository.ts`). The repository code does not change.

`TicketsService.findAll(slug, filters: TicketListFilterInput, page)` already forwards `filters.titleContains` to `PrismaTicketsRepository.findTicketPage`. That method applies `{ contains, mode: 'insensitive' }` to `title`. The koda agent tool (`fleet/assistant/tools/ticket-tools.ts`) is its only caller today.

After the API contract change, `bun run generate` from the repo root regenerates `openapi.json` and the CLI client. Check that the regenerated diff carries only the `search` change; drift from an outdated checkout is not part of this story. Include the specified 400-description update, not unrelated contract drift. Never hand-edit `apps/cli/src/generated/types.gen.ts`. Preserve existing guards, resolveSelfAssignee, JsonResponse pagination and repository behavior.

**Scope** — In: DTO/controller mapping, filter type and three comments, existing endpoint/controller tests, generated OpenAPI/CLI artifacts. Out: palette consumers (US-006/US-007), web not-found/navigation work (US-002–US-005), schema changes. A CLI flag for the new `search` query: the generated client is only regenerated. An index for the title search: it is the repository's existing whole-column `contains`, bounded here by a 2-character minimum, a 250 ms debounce and a page size of 8. `%` and `_` in `search`: they mean whatever the existing `titleContains` query gives them, the same as the koda tool search.

**Interface**
```ts
@ApiPropertyOptional({ maxLength: 100, description: 'Case-insensitive substring of the ticket title' })
@IsOptional()
@IsString()
@MaxLength(100)
search?: string;

export type TicketListFilterInput = Omit<ListTicketsQuery, 'current' | 'size' | 'search'> & { assignedToAgentId?: string; titleContains?: string };
```

**Test implementation** — AC-1 to AC-6 run in a new `describe` in section 13 of `endpoint.e2e.spec.ts`. In its own `beforeAll` it creates a new project with its own member, granted through `grantRole`/`grantBaseline` as the api-testing rule requires. That project holds exactly three tickets: `Fix Login button` (priority `HIGH`), `Login page copy` (priority `LOW`) and `Logout crash` (priority `HIGH`). Tickets other sections create in the shared project never appear in these results. Add AC-7 and AC-8 next to the existing `findAll` unit tests. Those assert with `expect.objectContaining` and stay unchanged. Every existing endpoint case stays unchanged. Use Vitest and the shared DB gate; execute DB cases outside the sandbox through host testScoped, not as skipped verification.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given the isolated three-ticket project, GET /api/projects/:slug/tickets?search=LOGIN returns 200 with exactly the two tickets Fix Login button and Login page copy.
[integration] Given the isolated three-ticket project, GET /api/projects/:slug/tickets?search=%20login%20 returns the same two tickets as search=login.
[integration] Given the isolated three-ticket project, GET /api/projects/:slug/tickets?search=%20%20 returns all three tickets.
[integration] Given the isolated three-ticket project, GET /api/projects/:slug/tickets?search=login&priority=HIGH returns exactly Fix Login button.
[integration] GET /api/projects/:slug/tickets with a search of 101 characters returns 400.
[integration] GET /api/projects/:slug/tickets with a search of 100 characters returns 200.
[unit] TicketsController.findAll('koda', { search: ' login ' }) calls TicketsService.findAll with filters whose titleContains is login and which have no search key.
[unit] TicketsController.findAll('koda', {}) calls TicketsService.findAll with filters that have no titleContains key.

routing.reasoning: This is an additive DTO/controller mapping onto an already implemented service/repository filter, with existing test and generation paths; role-bound fixtures reuse existing helpers and no authentication or authorization implementation changes.

add the AC-7 and AC-8 cases next to the existing `findAll` tests. Those assert with `expect.objectContaining` and stay unchanged.

userStories.title: Show a dedicated ticket-not-found state
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Render a localized, non-retryable ticket-not-found state for the primary ticket fetch's 404 failures.

**Motivation** — Retrying cannot help.

**Approach** — Apply these Design requirements verbatim:
- New `apps/web/components/NotFoundState.vue`, with props `title: string`, `body?: string`, `backTo: string` and `backLabel: string`. It renders:
  - `div data-testid="not-found-state"` (`text-center py-12`);
  - `h1 data-testid="not-found-title"` with `title`;
  - `p.text-muted-foreground data-testid="not-found-body"` with `body`, rendered only when `body` is set;
  - a `NuxtLink data-testid="not-found-back"` to `backTo`, reading `backLabel`.

  It has no Retry.
- `apps/web/pages/[project]/tickets/[ref].vue`.
  - Baseline: the ticket `useAsyncData` fetcher is `() => $api.get(apiPath\`/projects/${slug}/tickets/${ref}\`)`. The template branches are `LoadingState` (pending), `ErrorState` (error), then the ticket grid.
  - Target: the fetcher awaits the same call in a `try`. A rejection for which `isNotFoundError` is true resolves `null`. Any other rejection is rethrown.
  - Target: `ticketNotFound = computed(() => !pending.value && !error.value && ticketData.value === null)`. Nuxt 4 starts `data` as `undefined`, so `null` only ever means not found.
  - Target: a new branch after `ErrorState`, `<NotFoundState v-else-if="ticketNotFound">`, with:
    - `title` `t('tickets.notFound.title')`;
    - `body` `t('tickets.notFound.body', { ref })`;
    - `back-to` `` `/${slug}` ``;
    - `back-label` `t('tickets.notFound.back')`.

Failure Handling: The ticket fetch fails with anything other than a 404: it is rethrown, and the page keeps showing `ErrorState` with Retry, as today.

Add these exact values to both locale files:
| key | en | zh |
| tickets.notFound.title | Ticket not found | 工单不存在 |
| tickets.notFound.body | {ref} does not exist in this project, or it was deleted. | 此项目中不存在 {ref}，或它已被删除。 |
| tickets.notFound.back | Back to board | 返回看板 |

**Scope** — In: NotFoundState, primary ticket fetch normalization, strict-null computed, template branch, ticket translations and state/page tests. Out: global project route checking (US-003), document titles and AppErrorPage's full-page 404 (US-005), palette/API search. The HTTP status of the ticket not-found state: it stays 200, because only the project check aborts navigation. Not-found states on other detail pages (thread, fleet job, job logs, repo config): unchanged. Flows and schedules already have their own. Do not change live deletion behavior, secondary fetches or permission controls.

**Interface**
```ts
defineProps<{ title: string; body?: string; backTo: string; backLabel: string }>()
```
Use US-002's `isNotFoundError(err: unknown): boolean` in the real page fetcher; do not duplicate classification.

**Test implementation** — Create `tests/pages/ticket-not-found.spec.ts` for AC-1 to AC-7 and `tests/components/not-found-state.spec.ts` for AC-8 to AC-11. AC-1 to AC-7 mount the real ticket page with route `{ project: 'web', ref: 'WEB-404' }`. `NotFoundState`, `ErrorState` and `LoadingState` are stubbed and their props recorded. A `useAsyncData` stub records each fetcher by key and returns the `data`, `pending` and `error` refs the AC names. The mount passes `alias: { '~/composables/useApi': apiModule }`, so the `ApiError` the test constructs is the class `isNotFoundError` checks, and it aliases the page's child components to inert stubs as `ticket-detail-grid.spec.ts` does. Existing ticket page mounts start their ticket `useAsyncData` pending (`fakeAsyncData`) or with a loaded ticket, so none of them reaches the new not-found branch.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] When the real ticket page is mounted for project web and ref WEB-404, the fetcher recorded for key ticket-web-WEB-404 resolves null when $api.get rejects with new ApiError(40004, 'gone').
[unit] That ticket fetcher rejects with the same error object when $api.get rejects with new ApiError(50000, 'down').
[unit] With the ticket useAsyncData returning data null, pending false and error null, the real ticket page renders one NotFoundState whose title is t('tickets.notFound.title').
[unit] In that not-found ticket mount, NotFoundState back-to is /web.
[unit] In that not-found ticket mount, NotFoundState body is t('tickets.notFound.body', { ref: 'WEB-404' }).
[unit] With the ticket useAsyncData returning data null and a non-null error, the page renders ErrorState.
[unit] In that error mount, the page renders no NotFoundState.
[unit] NotFoundState mounted with title Gone, back-to /web and back-label Back renders Gone in [data-testid="not-found-title"].
[unit] In that NotFoundState mount, [data-testid="not-found-back"] is a link whose to is /web.
[unit] In that NotFoundState mount, [data-testid="not-found-back"] reads Back.
[unit] NotFoundState mounted without body renders no [data-testid="not-found-body"] element.

routing.reasoning: A small state component and a localized existing-page branch reuse the established classifier; primary-fetch normalization is bounded and does not change access control or live behavior.

suggestedCriteria: When the ticket useAsyncData has data undefined, pending false and error null, the page renders no NotFoundState.
When the ticket useAsyncData is pending with data null and error null, the page renders LoadingState.
NotFoundState mounted with a non-empty body renders that body in [data-testid="not-found-body"].
[unit] Given a non-404 primary ticket fetch error, invoking the rendered ErrorState's retry listener calls the ticket useAsyncData refresh(), preserving Retry behavior, as today.

userStories.title: Render the full-page 404 and descriptive document titles
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add localized full-page 404 presentation and reactive titles from shared headings, ticket state and error headings.

**Motivation** — Almost every page's browser title is the bare word "Koda" (F20).

**Approach** — Apply these Design requirements verbatim:
- `apps/web/components/AppErrorPage.vue`.
  - Baseline: a 503 branch (unavailable, Retry) and a generic branch (`errorPage.generic.title` with the status code, Go to home).
  - Target: a new `v-else-if="error.statusCode === 404"` branch between them, containing:
    - `h1 data-testid="error-page-not-found-title"` with `t('errorPage.notFound.title')`;
    - `p.text-muted-foreground data-testid="error-page-not-found-body"` with `t('errorPage.notFound.body')`;
    - the same `error-page-home` button, which calls `goHome`.

    It has no Retry. The component also calls `useHead`, whose `title` is `${heading} · Koda`. `heading` is `t('errorPage.unavailable.title')` for 503, `t('errorPage.notFound.title')` for 404, and `t('errorPage.generic.title', { statusCode })` otherwise.
- `apps/web/pages/[project]/tickets/[ref].vue`.
  - Target: the page calls `useHead(() => ({ title: pageTitle.value }))`, where `pageTitle` is:
    - `${ticket.ref} ${ticket.title} · Koda` when the ticket is loaded;
    - `${t('tickets.notFound.title')} · Koda` when `ticketNotFound`;
    - `${ref} · Koda` otherwise, using the route ref.
- `apps/web/components/PageHeader.vue`: the props object is kept (`const props = defineProps<...>()`), and the component calls `useHead(() => ({ title: \`${props.title} · Koda\` }))`. Every page that renders a `PageHeader` gets a title from its heading. The `ApprovalBadge` `titleTemplate` still adds its count prefix.

The current checkout's PageHeader has an unassigned defineProps call; bind its result as const props when implementing this target. Do not set a new titleTemplate or alter ApprovalBadge.

Add these exact values to both locale files:
| key | en | zh |
| errorPage.notFound.title | Page not found | 页面不存在 |
| errorPage.notFound.body | This page or project does not exist, or it was removed. | 该页面或项目不存在，或已被删除。 |

**Scope** — In: AppErrorPage 404 branch, PageHeader/ticket/error-page titles, localized 404 copy and existing regression-test adjustments. Out: project middleware/cache (US-003), ticket-fetch/state implementation (US-004), all palette/API work, changes to the ApprovalBadge prefix. The thread detail pages' titles (the bare thread title, with no "· Koda"): unchanged. Adding the project name to project sub-page titles. Checking the SSR HTTP status of `/nope-404`, the browser tab titles, and the palette in a real browser: a post-deploy manual check on koda-wk, not a story.

**Interface**
```ts
useHead(() => ({ title: pageTitle.value }))
useHead(() => ({ title: `${props.title} · Koda` }))
```
AppErrorPage keeps its existing error prop and goHome calls `clearError({ redirect: '/' })`. Titles must react to heading/ticket state rather than capture a one-time value.

**Test implementation** — Add AC-1 to AC-5 to `tests/components/app-error-page.spec.ts`. The tests "AC-10 generic error renders translated title", "post-review B5: the generic title renders through the real translator in both locales" and "AC-11 home clears error and redirects home" mount `statusCode: 404`. 404 now has its own branch, so those three mounts change to `statusCode: 500`, and B5 expects `['Something went wrong (500)', '发生错误（500）']`. The invariant: the generic branch renders `errorPage.generic.title` with the status code through the real translator in both locales, and its home button still redirects home. The 503 tests stay unchanged. The additional generic-title, generic-home and 503-Retry regression acceptance criteria are exercised by these retained tests, not by replacing them.

Create `tests/components/page-titles.spec.ts` for AC-6 to AC-13. AC-6 to AC-13 supply a recording `useHead` through `globals`. Each evaluates the title of the last recorded input, calling it first when it is a function. AC-13 mounts the board page through `mountSfc`, with `PageHeader` in `components` set to `loadSfc(webFile('components', 'PageHeader.vue'), sameGlobals)`. That is the real component, loaded with the same recording `useHead`, not the `uiStubs` stub. Ticket page mounts alias the page's child components to inert stubs as `ticket-detail-grid.spec.ts` does, so a partial ticket fixture such as `{ ref, title }` renders. US-003 supplies the default useHead harness stub; tests under this story override it for observation.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] AppErrorPage mounted with { statusCode: 404 } shows t('errorPage.notFound.title') in [data-testid="error-page-not-found-title"].
[unit] In that 404 mount, [data-testid="error-page-not-found-body"] shows t('errorPage.notFound.body').
[unit] In that 404 mount, clicking [data-testid="error-page-home"] calls clearError with { redirect: '/' }.
[unit] In that 404 mount, no [data-testid="error-page-retry"] element is rendered.

[unit] PageHeader mounted with title Labels records a title of Labels · Koda.
[unit] The ticket page, with the ticket loaded as { ref: 'WEB-7', title: 'Fix login' }, records a title of WEB-7 Fix login · Koda.
[unit] The ticket page, with the ticket useAsyncData returning data null, pending false and error null, records a title of t('tickets.notFound.title') followed by ' · Koda'.

[unit] AppErrorPage mounted with { statusCode: 503 } records a title of t('errorPage.unavailable.title') followed by ' · Koda'.
[unit] AppErrorPage mounted with { statusCode: 500 } records a title of t('errorPage.generic.title', { statusCode: 500 }) followed by ' · Koda'.
[unit] pages/[project]/index.vue, mounted for project web with the real PageHeader, records a title of web · Koda.

routing.reasoning: Shared reactive title calls and a standard conditional error branch use existing Nuxt patterns; the broad PageHeader impact is bounded by the upstream harness default and real-component seam tests.

suggestedCriteria: When PageHeader title changes from Labels to Agents, its recorded reactive head input yields Agents · Koda.
When a mounted ticket page's loaded ticket title changes from Fix login to Fix logout, its recorded reactive head input yields WEB-7 Fix logout · Koda.

[unit] AppErrorPage mounted with statusCode 500 through the real translators renders h1 titles ['Something went wrong (500)', '发生错误（500）'] for en and zh, preserving the generic branch's status-code interpolation in both locales.
[unit] When the generic 500 branch's error-page-home button is clicked, clearError receives { redirect: '/' }, preserving the existing home action.

The invariant: the generic branch renders `errorPage.generic.title` with the status code through the real translator in both locales, and its home button still redirects home. Add this story's AC-1 to AC-5 to this file. The 503 tests stay unchanged.

userStories.title: Jump to typed ticket references from the palette
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Parse typed ticket refs and offer a first-position jump to the matching loaded project.

**Motivation** — Typing `SB-1` shows "No matches".

**Approach** — Apply these Design requirements verbatim:
- New `apps/web/lib/palette-tickets.ts`:
  - `PALETTE_TICKET_SEARCH_MIN = 2`, `PALETTE_TICKET_SEARCH_SIZE = 8`, `PALETTE_TICKET_SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS = 250`;
  - `parseTicketRefQuery(query: string): { key: string; number: number } | null`. It trims the query and matches `/^([A-Za-z]+)-(\d+)$/`. It returns the upper-cased letters and the parsed integer. It returns `null` when there is no match, when the digits are more than 9, or when the number is `0`.
- `apps/web/components/CommandPalette.vue`.
  - Baseline: the search box uses `v-model="query"`. `results` filters `commands` by label and hint. The local `Project` type has `id`, `name` and `slug`.
  - Target, input: the search box uses `:value="query"` and `@input="onQueryInput"`, where `onQueryInput(e: Event)` sets `query` from `(e.target as HTMLInputElement).value`. The behavior is the same, and the mount harness can type into it.
  - Target, project type: `Project` gains `key: string`, and its `id` becomes `string | number` (the API sends a string id).
  - Target, ref command: `refCommand` is a computed. When `parseTicketRefQuery(query)` returns `{ key, number }` and a loaded project has `key === parsed.key`, it is `{ id: 'ticket-ref', label: t('palette.openTicket', { ref: \`${key}-${number}\` }), hint: project.name, icon: Ticket, run: go(\`/${project.slug}/tickets/${key}-${number}\`) }`. Otherwise it is `null`.

For a non-empty query, prepend refCommand when non-null to the existing static/project label-and-hint matches; for an empty query return commands as today. US-007 will later append ticketResults after those matches. Keep existing permission-gated destinations, ordering, keyboard navigation, go()/close() behavior and theme toggle unchanged. `/projects` returns `ProjectResponseDto[]`, which carry `id`, `name`, `slug` and `key` (the ref prefix). `TICKET_REF_PATTERN = /^([A-Z]+)-(\d+)$/` in `apps/api/src/common/utils/ticket-ref.util.ts`: a ref prefix is upper-case letters only. The new parser accepts lowercase input and normalizes before navigation; it does not change the backend parser.

Add/change these exact values in both locale files:
| key | en | zh |
| palette.openTicket | Open ticket {ref} | 打开工单 {ref} |
| palette.description | Search pages, projects and tickets, then press Enter to open. | 搜索页面、项目和工单，按回车打开。 |
| palette.placeholder | Type a page, project or ticket… | 输入页面、项目或工单… |

**Scope** — In: palette-tickets helper and constants, input handler, Project type, refCommand/result composition, translations and real-palette tests. Out: debounced title requests/loading state (US-007), REST query (US-001), not-found/titles (US-002–US-005), fetching ticket existence before jumping. Palette ticket search across projects, by description or by ref number, and past the first 8 results. This excludes cross-project title search, not the specified ref jump: a ref jump may match any project already returned by /projects.

**Interface**
```ts
export const PALETTE_TICKET_SEARCH_MIN = 2
export const PALETTE_TICKET_SEARCH_SIZE = 8
export const PALETTE_TICKET_SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS = 250
export function parseTicketRefQuery(query: string): { key: string; number: number } | null
```
`onQueryInput(e: Event)` uses `(e.target as HTMLInputElement).value`; the existing Command shape remains unchanged.

**Test implementation** — Create `tests/lib/palette-tickets.spec.ts` for AC-1 to AC-4 and `tests/components/command-palette-ticket-ref.spec.ts` for AC-5 to AC-7 and the empty-query regression criterion. AC-5 to AC-7 and that regression mount the real `CommandPalette.vue` with `open: false`, then call `setProps({ open: true })` and flush with `await Promise.resolve()` plus `nextTick()` (never `setImmediate`), so the palette's `open` watcher loads `/projects`. The spec defines `globalThis.HTMLInputElement` as an empty class in `beforeAll` and restores the previous value in `afterAll`, because the watcher's focus line reads it and Jest runs in the `node` environment. Every `onInput` call is followed by the same flush. Typing calls the search box's `onInput` handler with `{ target: { value } }`. `$api.get` for `/projects` resolves `[{ id: 'p1', name: 'Sandbox', slug: 'sandbox', key: 'SB' }, { id: 'p2', name: 'Web', slug: 'web', key: 'WEB' }]`. The palette specs that copy the component and replace `v-model="query"` with `:value="query"` still work: once the component uses `:value="query"`, the replace is a no-op and every existing assertion stands.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] parseTicketRefQuery(' sb-12 ') returns { key: 'SB', number: 12 }.
[unit] parseTicketRefQuery('SB-') returns null.

userStories.title: Search current-project ticket titles in the palette
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add bounded, debounced ticket-title search to the current project's palette with stale-response protection.

**Motivation** — The Cmd+K palette finds no tickets (F10).

**Approach** — Apply these Design requirements verbatim:
- `apps/web/components/CommandPalette.vue`.
  - Target, title search: `ticketResults` (`Command[]`) and `searching` (`boolean`) are refs, and a `requestSeq` counter starts at 0. A `watch(query)` handler cancels the debouncer, empties `ticketResults` and sets `searching` false. It then arms a new search only when all of these hold:
    - `props.projectSlug` is set;
    - the trimmed query is at least `PALETTE_TICKET_SEARCH_MIN` long;
    - `parseTicketRefQuery(query)` is `null`.

    The handler also increments `requestSeq` on every query change, before deciding whether to arm, so a response to an earlier query can never be applied. Arming sets `searching` true and triggers a `createDebouncer(runTicketSearch, PALETTE_TICKET_SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS)`.
  - Target, the search request: `runTicketSearch` takes `seq = ++requestSeq` and the trimmed query `q`. It calls `$api.get(apiPath\`/projects/${slug}/tickets\`, { query: { search: q, size: PALETTE_TICKET_SEARCH_SIZE } })`.
    - On success it maps `records` to `{ id: \`ticket-${t.id}\`, label: \`${t.ref} ${t.title}\`, hint: t('palette.ticket'), icon: Ticket, run: go(\`/${slug}/tickets/${t.ref}\`) }`.
    - On failure the result is an empty list, with no toast.
    - The result and `searching = false` apply only when `seq === requestSeq`.
  - Target, closing: closing the palette (`open` becomes false) cancels the debouncer, increments `requestSeq`, empties `ticketResults` and sets `searching` false.
  - Target, `results`: for a non-empty query, `results` is `[refCommand (when non-null), ...static matches as today, ...ticketResults]`. For an empty query it is `commands` as today.
  - Target, list items: while `searching` is true, the list shows `li data-testid="palette-searching"` with `t('palette.searching')`. The `palette.empty` item shows only when `results` is empty and `searching` is false.

The mapping's ticket record variable must not shadow the translator `t`; keep its label/hint semantics exactly as specified. Use `createDebouncer(fn, ms): { trigger, cancel }` from `apps/web/lib/debounce.ts` (trailing edge). US-006 supplies `PALETTE_TICKET_SEARCH_MIN = 2`, `PALETTE_TICKET_SEARCH_SIZE = 8`, `PALETTE_TICKET_SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS = 250` and `parseTicketRefQuery`. Use `apiPath` to encode interpolated segments and US-001's REST `search` query, consuming the existing paginated `records` envelope.

Failure Handling:
- A palette title search fails: it shows no ticket results and no toast, and the palette keeps working for its other entries.
- A palette search response arrives after the query changed: it is dropped. (Closing also bumps `requestSeq`; reopening resets the query, which empties the results.)

Add these exact values in both locale files:
| key | en | zh |
| palette.ticket | Ticket | 工单 |
| palette.searching | Searching tickets… | 正在搜索工单… |

**Scope** — In: debouncer/search refs/sequence guard, current-project wire request and command mapping, closing cleanup, result/loading composition, translations and real-palette async tests. Out: helper/ref/input implementation (US-006), API implementation/generation (US-001), not-found/titles (US-002–US-005), Palette ticket search across projects, by description or by ref number, and past the first 8 results. An index for the title search: it is the repository's existing whole-column `contains`, bounded here by a 2-character minimum, a 250 ms debounce and a page size of 8. `%` and `_` in `search`: they mean whatever the existing `titleContains` query gives them, the same as the koda tool search. Preserve all static/project commands and their permission gates.

**Interface**
```ts
export function createDebouncer(fn: () => void, ms: number): { trigger: () => void; cancel: () => void }
```
Wire request: `$api.get(apiPath\`/projects/${slug}/tickets\`, { query: { search: q, size: PALETTE_TICKET_SEARCH_SIZE } })`. The existing `Command` interface remains the output shape; initialize ticketResults to an empty Command array, searching to false, and requestSeq to 0. Invalidate before deciding whether a new request will ever run; guard both successful/failed results and final loading state.

**Test implementation** — Create `tests/components/command-palette-ticket-search.spec.ts`. Every AC mounts the real `CommandPalette.vue` with `open: false`, then calls `setProps({ open: true })` and flushes with `await Promise.resolve()` plus `nextTick()` (never `setImmediate`, which fake timers hold), so the `open` watcher loads `/projects`. The spec defines `globalThis.HTMLInputElement` as an empty class in `beforeAll` and restores it in `afterAll` (Jest runs in the `node` environment). It types by calling the search box's `onInput` handler with `{ target: { value } }` and flushes after every `onInput`, so the query watcher runs once per keystroke. It runs the 250 ms debounce with Jest fake timers. `$api.get` is a recording spy: `/projects` resolves `[{ id: 'p2', name: 'Web', slug: 'web', key: 'WEB' }]`, and `/projects/web/tickets` resolves `{ records: [{ id: 't1', ref: 'WEB-3', title: 'Fix login' }] }` unless the AC says otherwise. Existing specs do not pin results beyond unchanged static and project entries; do not weaken or replace them. Use deferred promises to prove responses are ignored even before any timer for a changed query advances.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] With projectSlug web, typing login in the real opened palette and advancing 250 ms calls $api.get with /projects/web/tickets and { query: { search: 'login', size: 8 } }.
[unit] After that request resolves, the palette renders an option with id ticket-t1.
[unit] In that search mount, the ticket-t1 option's label reads WEB-3 Fix login.
[unit] Activating the ticket-t1 option navigates to /web/tickets/WEB-3.
[unit] With projectSlug web, typing l and advancing 250 ms makes no /projects/web/tickets request.
[unit] With no projectSlug, typing login and advancing 250 ms makes no request to any path ending in /tickets.
[unit] With projectSlug web, typing lo and then login within 100 ms, then advancing 250 ms, makes exactly one /projects/web/tickets request.
[unit] In that debounced mount, that one request's search is login.
[unit] With projectSlug web, a /projects/web/tickets request for logi that resolves only after the query was changed to xyz, with no timer advanced after the change, adds no ticket-t1 option.
[unit] With projectSlug web, a /projects/web/tickets request for logi that resolves only after the query was changed to l, with no timer advanced after the change, adds no ticket-t1 option.
[unit] With projectSlug web and /projects/web/tickets rejecting, typing login and settling the request shows t('palette.empty').
[unit] In that failed-search mount, no option id starts with ticket-.
[unit] With projectSlug web, typing zzz-q and advancing 250 ms while /projects/web/tickets has not yet resolved renders [data-testid="palette-searching"].
[unit] With projectSlug web, typing WEB-3 and advancing 250 ms makes no /projects/web/tickets request.
[unit] When an in-flight palette search response arrives after the palette closes, it adds no ticket option.

routing.reasoning: The sequence guard and close/query cleanup are bounded local state in one existing component using the existing debouncer and upstream REST contract; deferred-promise and fake-timer tests cover the races without a new abstraction or integration layer.

suggestedCriteria: With projectSlug web, typing ' login ' sends search 'login' in the ticket request.
When a stale request settles while a newer search remains pending, [data-testid="palette-searching"] remains rendered.
When the palette closes before the 250 ms debounce expires, no ticket request is issued.
When searching is true and results is empty, the palette renders no palette.empty message.
[unit] When a palette title search fails, no toast is emitted.

[unit] Given projectSlug web and query web, when the ticket-title request fails, activating either the existing board command or project-p2 command navigates to /web, preserving navigation through the palette's other entries.
[unit] When the palette reopens after a previous search, the search input's value is '', reflecting the reset query.
